name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for one week first. This gives us real-world data on false positives and edge cases without disrupting workflows. The trade-off is delayed immediate feedback, but we avoid breaking trust with the team by applying changes blindly. After the week, we’ll have hard numbers to decide if full auto-apply is safe.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode won’t catch the *real* risk: PR-Agent’s false negatives—where it misses critical issues that humans catch. A week of silent failures teaches us nothing about what we’re *not* seeing. Instead, run a parallel review cycle where PR-Agent flags issues but humans still make the final call; that way we measure both false positives *and* false negatives before trusting automation. Settle it by comparing the two approaches on a single high-risk PR—if PR-Agent misses more than 20% of human-flagged issues, it’s not ready.
